title: No src module may run work on import — src/ AND src/utils/
note: Nine flat scripts (10a 10d 10e 10h 11c 13 14b 28 29) had no __main__ guard, so importing one ran it and rewrote outputs/ — a linter, language server or agent inspecting the tree would do it without meaning to. Fixed 2026-09-03 by tools/apply_main_guards.py wrapping each body in main(). Verified byte-identical outputs either side on 10a 10d 10h 14b 28; Script 29 moves by 4.5e-10 relative, floating-point only. D-120. WIDENED THE SAME DAY, on Martin's instruction, from a grep over src/*.py to import_audit --static over src/ AND src/utils/. The narrow glob could never have seen the file that prompted it: utils/mask_streams_to_land.py was a SCRIPT living in src/utils/, unguarded, and raising on import only because its committed sandbox path did not exist. --static reads the source rather than running it: a module fails if its TOP LEVEL carries a loop, a with, or a non-bootstrap call statement while having no __main__ guard. It is the cheap half of the audit and says so — a module doing I/O inside a top-level ASSIGNMENT (DF = pd.read_csv(...)) passes this and would fail the real one. The real audit is import_audit with no flag: it imports every module behind a write tripwire, takes many minutes against task_lint's TIMEOUT of 120 s, and so cannot be a standing check — a row calling it records 'timed out', which task_lint treats as an error and never as a pass. CURRENTLY 1, NOT 0: src/utils/paths.py calls DIR_nn.mkdir() at module level for Scripts 36, 37, 37b, 38, 39, 40 and 41 — seven directories created under outputs/ by the act of importing paths, which every module does. Harmless in effect (mkdir on an existing directory is a no-op) and inconsistent rather than wrong: every other DIR_ constant leaves creation to make_all_dirs(). Removing them is a one-line-each change to the most-imported module in the project and needs checking that those seven scripts call make_all_dirs() first — MARTIN'S CALL, and the reason this row is open rather than done. Do NOT use import_audit's own summary line: on this machine every module logs os.open /dev/null at import, so '0 clean' is unreachable and the count stays 93.
